primary_claim: A Large Concept Model (LCM), which predicts sentence-level embeddings rather than tokens, can predict future paragraphs of LLM-generated text well above baseline, with the most efficient (2-layer, 512-dim) model achieving 0.53 average cosine similarity to ground truth versus 0.51 for a Llama-3.2-1B LoRA baseline, and model size/architecture having little impact on performance (a 48x smaller model scores within 0.01 of the best model).

effect.metric: cosine similarity (SONAR embedding space) between predicted and actual paragraph
effect.value: Efficient Base-LCM 0.53, Best Base-LCM 0.54, Base-LCM re-implemented 0.525, Llama LoRA 0.51; first-paragraph-from-prompt: Base-LCM 0.78 vs Llama_t1 0.91

stated_future_work: try Diffusion-based LCM, which outperforms Base-LCM in the Meta paper
vary the level of document segmentation (sentences, paragraphs, sections)
use a more diverse dataset that includes sources other than documents to vary the structure of outputs
limitations_stated: variable-length outputs: evaluation truncates to target length, so the model is not penalised for poor quality of ignored later paragraphs
segmentation mismatch: naive index-wise cosine similarity penalizes correct outputs when semantic units are split across paragraph boundaries differently than the reference
quote: We aim to determine whether the LCM model — which predicts sentence embeddings rather than token embeddings — can predict the outputs of LLM. We compare four architectures, the most efficient model predicts the following paragraphs with a cosine similarity of 0.53.
